paper_metadata.title: Segregation behavior of alloying elements at Ni Σ 5 [001](210) symmetrical tilt grain boundary in nickel-based superalloys and their stabilization and strengthening mechanisms for the grain boundary

evidence.quote: Segregation behavior of alloying elements at Ni Σ 5 [001](210) symmetrical tilt grain boundary in nickel-based superalloys and their stabilization and strengthening mechanisms for the grain boundary

evidence.section: 2.1. Construction of the Ni Σ 5 [001](210) grain boundary model
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 1 (a) and (b), the coincidence site lattice (CSL) model of Ni Σ 5 [001](210) GB ( a = 3.523 Å, b = 7.878 Å and c = 26.056 Å) was established by mutually joining two tilt grains after rotating one grain 53.1° along the [001] axis, using the relaxed lattice constant of Ni unit cell.

evidence.section: 2.1. Construction of the Ni Σ 5 [001](210) grain boundary model
evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 1 (a) and (b), the coincidence site lattice (CSL) model of Ni Σ 5 [001](210) GB ( a = 3.523 Å, b = 7.878 Å and c = 26.056 Å) was established by mutually joining two tilt grains after rotating one grain 53.1° along the [001] axis, using the relaxed lattice constant of Ni unit cell.
All calculations were performed within the framework of density functional theory (DFT) by using the Vienna ab initio simulation package

evidence.quote: The GB energy ( γGB ) of the unsegregated Ni Σ 5 [001](210) GB we obtained is 1.27 J/m2
